## From Rio to Fernando de Noronha

In Rio de Janeiro, you will see Copacabana, Sugar Loaf, Corcovado and the city's old neighbourhoods. The next stop is Iguazu, with hundreds of waterfalls, tropical rainforest and the option to add the Argentine side, the Bird Park and the Macuco Safari to your itinerary.

The route gradually moves from big cities towards the ocean and islands. After Iguazu come Pernambuco, Recife and Olinda, with canals, bridges, colonial churches and traces of the Portuguese and Dutch periods. The pace then slows: Porto de Galinhas offers several days by warm waters, while Fernando de Noronha rounds off the trip with protected bays and marine wildlife.

The route then heads to northeastern Brazil. Recife is known for its canals, bridges and colonial architecture, while neighbouring Olinda has historic churches and panoramic views. Porto de Galinhas offers white sand, turquoise water, reefs and natural pools.

The final part of the journey takes place on Fernando de Noronha. The archipelago is known for its clear waters, beaches, dolphins, sea turtles and rich underwater life.
